references.text: The woman's response and Jesus' revelation of her life situation follow directly on his invitation. Jesus already knew the truth about her marriage and used this as a means to reveal his prophetic insight ([ref:Joh 4:17-18|John 4:17-18]).

Jesus' supernatural knowledge of people's lives is a recurring theme in the Gospel of John. Just as he knew Nathanael before they met, he also knows the situation of the Samaritan woman ([ref:Joh 1:48|John 1:48]).
John emphasizes that Jesus knew all people and knew what was in man—an insight clearly expressed in his conversation with the Samaritan woman ([ref:Joh 2:24-25|John 2:24-25]).

The woman later testifies to the townspeople, saying "he has told me everything I have done", which connects directly with Jesus' invitation to fetch her husband and the subsequent revelation ([ref:Joh 4:29|John 4:29]).

Jesus knew from the beginning who did not believe and who would betray him. His all-knowing knowledge of people is the same trait shown in the conversation with the Samaritan woman ([ref:Joh 6:64|John 6:64]).

Prophetic insight used to reveal hidden truths about people's lives has parallels in the Old Testament, such as when the prophet Ahijah saw through Jeroboam's wife who came disguised ([ref:1 Kong 14:6|1 Kings 14:6]).

The prophet Nathan's confrontation with David over his sin with Bathsheba is an Old Testament parallel where God's servant exposes hidden sin related to marriage and cohabitation ([ref:2 Sam 12:7|2 Samuel 12:7]).

Nothing in creation is hidden from God, but all things lie naked and bare before his eyes. This truth is illustrated concretely in Jesus' penetrating knowledge of the Samaritan woman's life ([ref:Hebr 4:13|Hebrews 4:13]).
